panels.title: Crawl health — did crawls run, complete, and did the oracle take part?
Explorer UP
panels.description: Prometheus scrape liveness. 0 = the explorer is unreachable and VerdictExplorerDown will fire after 3m. NOT derived from crawl activity — an idle explorer is still UP.

panels.title: Crawls started (24h)
panels.description: Did crawls run at all?

panels.title: Crawls completed (24h)
panels.description: Did they reach a terminal state? Every terminal outcome counts here, including failures — pair it with the failure panel.

panels.title: Crawl failure rate (30m)
panels.description: Are failures increasing? Alert VerdictCrawlFailureRateHigh fires above 25%.

panels.title: In-flight crawls
panels.description: Currently executing. Single-flight per container, so this equals the number of busy explorer replicas.

panels.title: ZERO-ORACLE crawls (24h)
panels.description: THE MILESTONE SIGNAL. Crawls that WIRED an oracle and reached a terminal state having never consulted it. These look healthy and are not: journeys were catalogued as samples. expected="no" only — a probe/observe crawl with no oracle wired is excluded.

panels.title: Crawl rate — started vs completed vs failed
panels.description: Started diverging above completed means crawls are starting and not finishing — the pipeline is wedged.

panels.title: Crawl failure rate over time
panels.description: The trend behind VerdictCrawlFailureRateHigh.

panels.title: Failures by class
panels.description: browser_launch ⇒ container/memory/shm. crawl_exception ⇒ read the correlated crawl_id from the qec.crawl.event logs.

panels.title: Crawls started by mode and posture
panels.description: traversal=full/e2e crawls are the ones that wire an oracle; probe and observe legitimately do not.

panels.title: Crawl duration percentiles
panels.description: p99 pinned at the wall budget (1800s default) means crawls are being cut off rather than finishing.

panels.title: Duration p95 by terminal reason
panels.description: Separates 'finished fast' from 'died fast'.

panels.title: Crawl depth — how far did they get?
Deepest depth ever reached
panels.description: High-water mark across the explorer process's lifetime.

panels.title: Mean max-depth (24h)
panels.description: Average deepest-depth per crawl. A fall here is coverage regressing.

panels.title: Max depth reached — percentiles
panels.description: Depth LEVELS (not seconds). p95 collapsing toward 0-1 means crawls stopped getting past the entry page.

panels.title: Depth distribution (24h, cumulative buckets)
panels.description: Cumulative histogram buckets: each bar is the number of crawls whose max depth was AT MOST that level.

panels.title: Depth trend by terminal reason
panels.description: Shallow + terminal_reason=completed is the suspicious pair: the crawl ran out of app, or ran out of the ability to advance.

panels.title: Terminal reasons — why did they stop?
Terminal reason breakdown (24h)
panels.description: Bounded vocabulary — an exception string can never appear here.

panels.title: Terminal reasons over time
panels.description: A rise in timeout / budget_max_states means crawls are being truncated rather than finishing.

panels.title: Timed out (24h)
panels.description: Crawls stopped by the wall-clock budget.

panels.title: Cancelled (24h)
panels.description: Operator-requested stops.

panels.title: Guard blocks (24h)
panels.description: Requests aborted by the fail-closed network guard.

panels.title: States visited (24h)
panels.description: Total unique states across all crawls.

panels.title: Oracle behaviour — did the oracle participate?
Oracle calls by outcome
panels.description: circuit_open and cap_reached are consultations REFUSED before reaching the wire — they do not count as oracle participation.

panels.title: Oracle failures by reason
panels.description: transport/timeout ⇒ qe-central unreachable. bad_body ⇒ the agent replied unreadably. circuit_open ⇒ the breaker gave up for this crawl.

panels.title: Oracle latency percentiles
panels.description: Approaching the 8s advance-oracle timeout means consultations are about to start failing.

panels.title: Oracle calls (24h)
panels.description: Total consultations across all oracle kinds.

panels.title: Oracle failures (24h)
panels.description: Consultations that produced no decision.

panels.title: Oracle success ratio (30m)
panels.description: Fraction of consultations that produced a usable decision.

panels.title: NO-ORACLE — crawls that reached a terminal state without invoking the oracle
Crawls completing with ZERO oracle calls
panels.description: THE failure mode this milestone exists to expose. The two series are deliberately separate: a probe-posture crawl legitimately makes zero oracle calls, and folding it in here would bury the real signal. The UNEXPECTED series is exactly the expression VerdictCrawlsCompletingWithoutOracle alerts on (threshold 0.002/s, for 15m).

targets.legendFormat: UNEXPECTED — oracle was wired and never called

panels.title: Zero-oracle crawls by terminal reason (24h)
panels.description: terminal_reason=completed with expected=no is the worst pair: a crawl that reported success without the oracle ever taking part.

panels.title: Zero-oracle share of all crawls (24h)
panels.description: What fraction of terminal crawls silently skipped the oracle.

panels.title: Crawls WITH oracle participation (24h)
panels.description: The healthy counterpart — the oracle answered at least once.

panels.title: Oracle participation state of terminal crawls
panels.description: used / unconfigured / configured_unused — the bounded three-state classification carried on every terminal crawl.

panels.title: Dispatch — is qe-central able to hand work to the explorer?
Dispatch attempts by outcome
panels.description: accepted / busy_409 / unauthorized / rejected. A wall of unauthorized means the fleet token is mismatched.

panels.title: Dispatch 409 (worker contention)
panels.description: The explorer is single-flight; a sustained 409 rate means the fleet is undersized or a crawl is wedged holding the slot. Alert VerdictExplorerDispatch409Spike fires above 0.05/s for 15m.

panels.title: Dispatches unauthorized (24h)
panels.description: Any non-zero value is a fleet-token misconfiguration.

panels.title: Token consumption — how expensive were the crawls?
Total tokens (24h)
panels.description: prompt + completion. Cache tokens are tracked separately and are deliberately NOT added in — they would double-count the same prompt.

panels.title: Estimated spend (24h)
panels.description: A SEPARATE concept from token count — populated only when a stable price table is configured. Zero here means no pricing is configured, never that the crawls were free.

panels.title: Tokens per crawl (24h avg)
panels.description: A sharp rise means an app is looping the oracle on one decision point.

panels.title: Token consumption over time
panels.description: Alert VerdictCrawlTokenBurnAnomalous fires above 500 tok/s for 20m.

panels.title: Tokens by model
panels.description: provider/model are cardinality-bounded: at most 50 distinct values are admitted per label, everything after folds into `other`.

panels.title: LLM calls by outcome
panels.description: error_with_usage = the provider billed us and then failed. Those tokens are counted, because a failed call is not a free one.

panels.title: qe-central LLM boundary — tokens by provider
panels.description: The same spend seen at the qe-central→platform-api boundary (T-OB-03). Divergence from the explorer-side view means LLM calls are being made for something other than a crawl.
